G5607.abbott_html: with various uses and significations, like the English verb to be. I. As substantive verb. 1. Of persons and things, to be, exist: al; ὁ ὢν καὶ ὁ ἦν (for past ptcp.); τὰ (μὴ) ὄντα. 2. Of times, events, etc. to be, happen, take place: al. 3. to be present, be in a place, have come: al. seq. εἰς; seq. ἐκ, (ἐξ), al. 4. Impers. ἔστι, ἦν, etc. (a) there is (Fr. il y a), was, etc. al. c. dat. (of the possessor; Bl. §37, 3), al. ἔστιν ὅς, ὅστις (chiefly in pl), al. (b) c. inf. = ἔξεστιν (q.v.), it is possible: RV (but v. ICC, in l.). II. As copula uniting subject and predicate. 1. Expressing simply identity or equivalence: al. mult. 2. Explicative, as in parable, figure, type, etc. al. τοῦτ’ ἔστιν, al. ὅ ἐστιν, al. akin to this is the sacramental usage. 3. C. gen. qual. etc. al. part. poss. of service or partisanship. 4. C. dat. (BL, §37, 3): al. 5. C. ptcp. as a periphrasis for the simple verb; (a) c. ptcp. pf. (cl.): al (b) c. ptcp. pr. (esp. in impf. as in Heb. and Aram. Dalman, Words, 35 f.), al. mult. id. for imper. with ellipsis of εἰμί, al. (c) c. ptcp. aor. (cl). 6. Seq. εἰς, a vernac. usage: al. 7. C. adv. al. 8. Ellipses; (a) of the copula: al. (b) of the predicate: ἐγώ εἰμί, al. absol. al.
